build: Two-sided English disk edition; G64 preservation images supplied by the contributor

extra: Opening dialogue with embedded control bytes
Opening messages and prompts; exact record boundaries remain open

comments.text: For up to X groups of sixty decrements of $030E, watch keyboard-queue growth and joystick state $030C. A new keyboard byte is removed when it aborts the wait. Before returning, wait for joystick fire to be released, set the fire latch, and clear the wheel-prefix length.

Outside scene $1A, decrement the frame subcounter $0373. On underflow reload $3B and borrow through seconds $0374, minutes $0375, and hours $0376; seconds and minutes reload to $3B. If hours underflow, clear $0580. The real-time rate depends on the IRQ path that calls this routine and is measured separately.
Wait until the IRQ-maintained counter at $0353 reaches ten, clear it, and return. This paces the main graphical loop; it is not a disk-transfer wait.

Save A, X, and Y; select I/O with processor-port value $25; arm the raster chain through $1267; acknowledge VIC and CIA interrupts, update counters, and call frame services before restoring the saved banking and registers. The individual service purposes remain open.
RTI is the complete NMI target held in $FFFA/$FFFB in the opening snapshot.
Set raster compare to $3D, install $127C in the hardware IRQ vector, clear the border color, and return.

Copy six sprite X positions from $02CC-$02D1 and sprite attributes from RAM to VIC registers. Set the first six Y positions to $46, acknowledge the interrupt, schedule raster $50, and install $136F as the next handler.

Scan both CIA1 keyboard matrix ports, derive the row and column through $193F, and index the RAM key-translation table at $DCD6 with I/O banked out. Suppress the same key until release; recognized shifted states select the second 64-byte translation bank. Queue translated bytes through $18DB.
Append A to the 16-byte input queue at $02E0 when $02F2 is below sixteen. Mark the queue busy with $02DF=0 while updating, then set $02DF=$FF. A full queue drops the new byte.
Shift A left through carry for eight iterations. X counts zero bits, and $185D retains the row index of a one bit. The keyboard scanner combines two such scans to select a translated key.

Compare the accumulated joystick bits at $194E with $194F. On a change, convert direction bits into signed X and Y requests at $0308/$0309 and store the remaining fire bit in $030A. Clear the accumulator. A newly held fire button queues $FF through $18DB and is suppressed until release.
Set CIA1 port A as outputs high and port B as inputs, read control port 1, invert its active-low bits, mask to $1F, and store $030C. OR the sample into $194E for the main-loop direction/fire decoder.

Read track 18, sector 0 into $CB00. Compare the fifteen-character disk-name prefix against LABYRINTH SIDE, then decode its following digit. Return zero for a failed read, a mismatched prefix, or a decoded digit at least three. Otherwise return the digit.
Send the track and sector in X/Y with command $40 to the drive, then transmit the 256-byte page selected by $1BA1/$1BA2. Temporarily mask CIA2 interrupts around the serial transaction.

Send track and sector X/Y with command $30 to the drive, then receive escaped data through $1AB8 into the buffer configured at $1B9C-$1B9F. CIA2 interrupts are masked during the transaction; carry and $1BA0 report the receive outcome.

Send the two-character filename in X/Y with drive command $10, consume its two-byte PRG load address, and receive its payload into the configured buffer. The payload is placed at the caller's chosen destination, not the PRG's load address.

Receive bytes through $1B2A and write them through a self-modifying indexed store. Escape $01 followed by $01 emits a literal $01; $11 reports an error; $81 marks successful end of file. A plain payload byte advances the destination, and reaching the configured end page reports code $01 with carry set. Other escape values perform the block handshake and continue.
Set the serial port state, perform the drive-ready handshake, and send the request's two X/Y parameter bytes followed by the command byte originally in A.
Delay, wait for CIA2 port-A bit $40 to rise, acknowledge through $DD00, then delay again. These busy waits are part of the custom drive protocol.
Call the two-bit serial receiver at $1B3A four times and return the accumulated byte at $1B99.
Read CIA2 port A twice with the alternating acknowledge states $1C and $0C, shifting the sampled serial bit into $1B99 after each read. The intervening transfers preserve the protocol timing.
Store A at $1B99 and call the two-bit serial transmitter at $1B6A four times.
Rotate two successive high bits from $1B99 into the carry and select CIA2 port-A states $1C/$3C and $0C/$2C to transmit them, with fixed intervening instructions for timing.

Remember the requested disk number in A and repeatedly call $19CC until it matches. Show the appropriate insert/turn-disk message through $551B, wait for a keyboard-queue event through $5DE5, and retry. Transition autosaving can require the old side before the new side.
Load the two-character file cached at $508F/$5090 into $7900, with a buffer end at $8B00. Retry when the custom loader returns carry set. The opening setup selects AF for female and AV for male.
Load the file cached at $5091/$5092 into $E800 with end page $EB00, retrying on receive error. This buffer is separate from the packed room character data at $E000.
Load the two-character costume filename cached at $5093/$5094 into $A000 with end page $BC00. Retry on carry set. The scene setup chooses the filename through the character-type table at $5969.

Preserve the two-byte random state at $0502/$0503, clear pages $0400 and $0500, restore that state, and install initial progression values and $FF sentinels. Call $4210 once and save its returned state at $0501.

Write the $0400 and $0500 pages to two track-18 sectors selected by the active save slot at $6297, then update the slot-name state through $63E7. This is persistent game state, not the emulator snapshot format.
Read the active slot's two track-18 sectors into $0400 and $0500 using the sector tables at $5807/$580B, then refresh the change-log index and player-name display through $5871 and $622D.

Read the packed byte count and expanded byte count from a four-byte header. Move the packed block to the end of the configured buffer, then expand it back at its original destination. Tokens $00-$3F copy count+1 literals; $40-$7F repeat the following byte count+1 times; $80-$9F repeat zero; $A0-$BF repeat $55; $C0-$DF repeat $AA; $E0-$FF repeat $FF, using the low five bits plus one for these constant runs. Stop at the declared output end, even within a run. A separate decoder matched the live M2, P2, and C2 expansions byte for byte.

Service message-window timing, failure state, and the room hook at $8C8F, then dequeue at most one pending key. In graphical mode, scenes below two skip the wheel commands. $FF executes the chosen command, $FE clears the prefix, $FD/$FC move through choices, and $FB or Space changes the active wheel. Printable letters reach the typing path; the remaining filter tests the sign of X minus $20. $EF reaches the restart path.
Remember the keyboard-queue count, wait for it to change, and decrement it once. This waits for a newly queued key rather than accepting a key already in the queue.
Store $FF in $71-$74. These four runtime flags disable the four actor display slots until other code sets them again.
Wait until the queue-busy flag at $02DF is negative, take the first byte from $02E0 into X, shift the remaining entries down, and decrement the queued-byte count $02F2.

With $6666 clear, use signed delta X to search from the active selection, skipping entries with a negative $66FB flag. Zero or an index reaching $6679 restores the original selection. A selected change clears the prefix through $61F7. Redraw the active wheel and choose the right-hand wheel mode from the action table $66DC; $6666 can bypass the movement search.
Append A through $5F2C, then search the active wheel through $612C. Clear $6666 on return. The caller $5EED supplies a nonnegative key byte; command execution takes its separate negative-byte branch.

A is a typed byte. If prefix length $6682 equals ten, return unchanged. Otherwise store A at $6683 plus that length, subtracting $20 first when A is at least $5B; restore the original A and increment the prefix length. The guard tests equality with ten, not an arbitrary out-of-range length.

Resolve the selected action and right-hand word into dictionary indices $6691/$6692. Scan two-byte action/object pairs at $8B00 through offset $BE, treating zero in either field as a wildcard and a negative first field as an end marker. A match uses its parallel pointer at $8BC0: negative high bytes jump to code, otherwise set high bit and pass the message to $674C. In text mode, call $7903 before the response.

Y selects an entry in the combined wheel table and X selects a column offset in the $CF70 screen rows. Resolve its dictionary index through $6693, read the word using the hidden-RAM pointer halves $D900/$D800 with port $24 selected, and copy letters through $60AA. Pad to the configured wheel width. Inventory wheel two appends parentheses around entry value plus $31 for values one through nine; zero and values at least ten omit that suffix. The byte for value nine would be a colon, whose player reachability is open.

Match the uppercase prefix at $6683, length $6682, against available entries of the active wheel. A first letter starts at base plus one with $6679 candidates; a longer prefix starts at the selected slot with $6679 minus that slot candidates. Negative $66FB flags skip an entry. Fold word bytes at least $5B by subtracting $20. On success select the matching slot, highlight the new prefix position, and redraw through $5EB0. On failure write red ($02) to the border and decrement the prefix length, preserving the preceding accepted prefix and selection.

Set one colour cell to white ($01). Add the accepted prefix length to the active wheel column offset with the incoming carry, use the sum as Y, and write $DB97,Y. The successful search enters with carry set from subtracting the wheel base, so the addition includes one extra cell.
For the active wheel, set the existing prefix's colour cells to white ($01), walking backwards from the stored length at $6682. Return immediately for a zero length.

Restore fourteen colour cells beginning at $DB98 plus the active wheel's column offset to colour three, then set prefix length $6682 to zero. The selected word at $666D plus wheel number is preserved; the previously stored prefix bytes are left in the buffer.

Begin with Y=$FF so the shared parser at $67B7 advances to the stream's first byte. Zero flushes and ends; $FF flushes a line. $FB-$FE select dictionary-word substitutions, while $F6-$FA alter cursor or formatting state. The literal marker $40 is suppressed; other bytes pass to $6891.
Emit the pending formatting close byte at $691F when nonzero, clear it, advance the output line through $6A4E, and reset the current column from the left margin at $0342.

Subtract forty from the output pointer's low byte. The code computes a borrow from its high byte but does not store that high-byte result. In the text-adventure mode, also decrement the scrolling row count. Whether a boundary crossing is reachable requires a separate test.

Save Y, store the character at output pointer $99/$9A plus current column $6997, then add $0C00 to that pointer to write its color in visible color RAM with port $25 selected. Restore banking and the original text pointer, increment the column, and restore Y.

Read the word index after a $FB-$FE token. Bank I/O out with port $24; use the high-byte table $D800 and low-byte table $D900 to patch the source of an indexed LDA. Emit bytes until zero. A negative $6920 subtracts $20 from the first character; bit zero appends a space. Restore port $25 and resume the parent stream.

Load file TX at $7900, set up its text window, and call its entry at $7900. Then run the wheel handler $5D36 and the overlay's $8C8F service until $6995 becomes negative. Return to the graphical engine after that state change.

If the scrolling row count is fourteen, scroll through $6B2E when the mode flag allows it and return with carry set. Otherwise add forty to the text pointer, increment the row count in text-adventure mode, and return with carry clear.

Configure the VIC text-scroll value, copy the selected text-window color into four color bands, clear the text area, clear the wheel rows, reset its row and column counters, and set output pointer $99/$9A to $CCA0.
Move fourteen rows of text up one row using three copy loops, then fill 38 cells of the final row with spaces. This moves character codes; the text-window color bands are managed separately.

Opening dialogue contains literal ASCII mixed with bytes above $7F. Literal spans include the teenage moviegoers and their clothing. The high-byte substitutions and control bytes have not been decoded.
Literal ASCII fragment: You are standing on the sidewalk on. The sentence continues through encoded bytes beyond this fragment.
Literal ASCII heading: Welcome to Labyrinth, preceded by spaces.

Eight-byte monochrome glyphs at the printable ASCII positions. Rendering verifies digits at $30-$39, uppercase at $41-$5A, and lowercase at $61-$7A. Several punctuation slots and the slots beyond $7A are graphics or blank; see reference/opening-font.png.

Split dictionary pointers: 256 high bytes at $D800, then 256 low bytes at $D900. The stream parser indexes both with the byte after a $FB-$FE control. The table lives in RAM beneath I/O, read with port $24.
Low-byte half of the 256 dictionary pointers. The corresponding high byte for index X is at $D800+X; $68D4 combines these through a self-modifying LDA while RAM beneath I/O is visible.

Sixty-four keyboard matrix translations used by $18C6 with no shift-bank offset. Printable letters are lowercase ASCII; control values such as $FF for Return and $FD/$FC for cursor movement are interpreted by the word-wheel handler.
The second 64 keyboard translations, selected by the scanner shift-bank offset. Letters are uppercase ASCII; shifted cursor and function-key entries use their own control bytes.

The caller at $69E1-$69EE writes $24 to the processor port before this JSR and restores $25 afterwards. This routine therefore executes from RAM beneath I/O; its opening loop clears two 34-cell screen runs at $CCA2 and $CED2 with value $0A.
